headline: Chip rally unwinds: Nvidia falls 5.9% and Micron 11.0% as silver sinks to a 52-week low
subhead: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,201.1 and the Nasdaq 1.5% on tariff reports and a weak Analog Devices outlook; gold lost 3.1% to sit 0.7% above its 52-week low, and bitcoin fell 2.9% to 59,439.5.

us.text: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,201.1 and the Nasdaq 1.5% as chip stocks gave back Monday's rally; Nvidia lost 5.9%.
Micron fell 11.0% after a BNP Paribas downgrade, and Texas Instruments 11.3% after Analog Devices gave a weak outlook.
Reports of new US tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies added pressure ahead of PCE inflation data on 25 November.

india.text: On 23 Nov the Nifty fell 1.8% to 25,349.7 and Bank Nifty 3.2% as HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank each lost 3.3%.
FIIs bought a net Rs 5,673 crore and DIIs sold Rs 2,760 crore in the cash market on 23 Nov, provisional data show.
The rupee fell 30 paise to 92.92 per dollar on 23 Nov, ending a five-day winning streak as stocks slid.

global.text: Samsung Electronics fell 7.3% on 25 Nov as Seoul chip stocks slumped again, triggering a sidecar pause in program trading.
European shares ended lower on 24 Nov as the tech rally faded and miners slid; Sanofi jumped on a $41 billion Insmed deal.
Brent settled at $91.40 and WTI at $82.05 as reports of new tanker attacks overshadowed US-Iran diplomacy.

weekly.narrative: An AI unwind dominated the week: Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut failed to steady sentiment, Nvidia fell 22.9 percent and the Nasdaq 10.0 percent, its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6 percent and closed in correction. Near-certain bets on a December Fed hike pushed gold down 8.1 percent and silver 14.4 percent to near 52-week lows, and bitcoin fell 5.8 percent toward its 2026 low. India stood apart as heavy foreign buying lifted the Nifty to a nine-month high of 25,800.6 and Bank Nifty to records, while Tokyo, Seoul and Frankfurt followed Wall Street lower. Next week is shortened by Thanksgiving and turns on US PCE inflation and GDP on 25 November, ahead of the Fed decision on 9 December.
